glosses: An act of endearment; any act or expression of affection; an embracing, or touching, with tenderness.

examples.text: He exerted himself to win by indulgence and caresses the hearts of all who were under his command.
And he wooed her with his soft caresses, / Wooed her with his smile of sunshine, […]

glosses: A gentle stroking or rubbing.
To touch or kiss lovingly; to fondle.

examples.text: She loves being caressed by her boyfriend.

glosses: To affect as if with a caress.

examples.text: The love and anguish in his voice caressed my mind and soul.

glosses: The act or process of endearing, of causing (something or someone) to be loved or to be the object of affection.

examples.text: Every step of that walk led Jeff deeper into an excursion of endearment. It was amazingly true that he trod beside her an acknowledged friend, a secret lover.

glosses: The state or characteristic of being endeared.

examples.text: He could not forget the fond and earnest look that had passed between her and some other man—the attitude of familiar confidence, if not of positive endearment.

glosses: An expression of affection.

examples.text: When they were alone he called him "my boy," an endearment he never gave another.

glosses: A tendency to express warm, compassionate feelings.

examples.text: When the lovers were together, their cold indifference gave way to love and tenderness.

I had known him jealous, suspicious; I had seen about him certain tendernesses, fitfulnesses—a softness which came like a warm air, and a ruth which passed like early dew, dried in the heat of his irritabilities: this was all I had seen.

glosses: A concern for the feelings or welfare of others.

examples.text: When they saw the poor orphans, they were overwhelmed with tenderness for them.
Everybody needs a little tenderness sometimes.

examples.text: He noted her extreme tenderness when he touched the bruise on her thigh.
